subject: Provisional standby activation window request — Federated Bank EU
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@federatedbank.com>, Procurement <procurement@federatedbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Provisional standby activation window request — Federated Bank EU

Hi Elena / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the detailed call yesterday. After reviewing Federated Bank's regulatory requirements and the architecture constraints for your multi-region deployment, we need to request a temporary, measured exception to the multi-region RTO commitment while we deliver a warm-standby upgrade in the Amsterdam region.

What we're asking for (provisional):
- Temporary standby activation window: up to 4 hours RTO for cross-region switchover during the 90-day migration window.
- RPO: unchanged (no customer data loss expected; KV prefix caching will be preserved for warm nodes).
- Mitigations: short-term scaled-read replicas in FR, rolling canary tests, and an automated rollback policy to single-region traffic if health checks fail.

Why we need the window:
- Your current configuration includes encrypted cold backups and an initial warm layer that needs kernel/quantization tuning to meet sub-30min cross-region activation at the scale in question. We're proposing a staged rollout to hit the full SLA without introducing risk.

Attachments: federated-tech-runbook.pdf (technical runbook), redwood-interim-terms.pdf (provisional terms). I attached a canary scope spreadsheet for the tests we discussed.

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm whether Procurement can accept a 90-day provisional amendment to the Master Services Agreement with the standby window described above.
2) Approve the canary scope so engineering can schedule tests the week of July 2.
3) If accepted, we'll provide a daily status cadence and an executive notification plan.

Happy to hop back on a quick call to walk through specifics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — quick technical notes to support the request:

1) Root cause for longer RTO across regions is primarily cold KV-cache rehydration for large session state footprints. We can reduce the operational impact by:
   - Pre-warming the KV cache on a rolling basis for high-risk prefixes.
   - Enabling prefix-based sticky caching for active customers during the transition window.
2) We should define explicit canary acceptance criteria:
   - 95th percentile end-to-end latency for generation calls remains under 450ms for canary subset (10% traffic)
   - Successful KV rehydrate within 180s for critical prefixes in 95% of attempts
3) Suggested timeline:
   - Week 1: Canary dry runs (non-prod-to-prod switchover rehearsals)
   - Week 2: Limited-production canary (10% traffic, live telemetry)
   - Week 3: Ramp to full production if metrics meet thresholds

I'll draft a brief ops-runbook excerpt to include in the interim terms that spells out rollback thresholds.

-Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

[Note: no new attachments in this reply]

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Provisional standby activation window request — Federated Bank EU

Thanks Marissa — and Karthik, appreciate the details. A few clarifying questions before Procurement signs off:

1) During the 4-hour window, what is the expected user-visible degradation? Will we see higher tail latency, partial failures, or queueing?
2) Who owns incident response for cross-region activation during the exception window (Federated duty team or Redwood Ops)? Need point-of-contact and on-call rotations.
3) For audit/compliance, we require an explicit rollback policy and daily evidence (logs/metrics) during the 90-day period. Can Redwood commit to that output format?

Procurement: please advise on contract language tolerances — is a time-bound, conditional amendment acceptable versus a permanent SLA change?

Elena
Director, Cloud Reliability
Federated Bank

Team — proposed commercial/operational compromise to present to Federated:

1) 90-day provisional amendment that explicitly states: standby activation RTO up to 4 hours for cross-region failover only; otherwise all other SLA terms remain unchanged.
2) Redwood provides daily health packets during the 90 days: JSON telemetry export and a 30-min summary dashboard for executive stakeholders. (We will link to the HubSpot record for traceability.)
3) If canary thresholds (Karthik's criteria) are met for 10 consecutive business days, the temporary window is rescinded and the standard multi-region RTO (sub-30min target) is reinstated with a pro-rated service credit for any deviations.
4) Contract amendment includes a one-page rollback and incident responsibilities matrix (Redwood leads activation; Federated has observer rights and escalation path).

Requesting: Mina and Marissa, please approve language and I'll loop Legal for a short addendum. Elena / Procurement — can you confirm acceptance of this approach in principle so we can prepare a DocuSign addendum?

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Engineering
jonas.weber@redwood.com
